newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin recovering slowly, plans more meetings.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovering slowly, plans more meetings.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is making a slow recovery from pneumonia and will not return to the Kremlin in the near future, his press secretary said on Tuesday.
"The rehabilitation goes rather slowly," Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing.

"Although the president is getting better little by little, including in his physical activity which is shown by the greater number of meetings and a more intense work schedule, I want to repeat that we should not expect a speedy return to the Kremlin," he said.
Yeltsin was taken to hospital with pneumonia on January 8, two weeks after his return to the Kremlin following a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5.
On Tuesday Yeltsin held his regular weekly meeting with Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin at the Gorky-9 country residence outside Moscow where he is recuperating.
Their talks focused on Chernomyrdin's visit last week to the United States and a planned summit next month in Helsinki between Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton.

"The Russian leadership expects a direct, detailed and even firm dialogue in Helsinki but nevertheless we can hope that the meeting will be successful and will be marked by major agreements," Yastrzhembsky said.

Despite disagreements with Washington -- particularly over NATO's planned expansion to incorporate former communist countries in central and eastern Europe -- Chernomyrdin gave Yeltsin a positive assessment of bilateral relations.
"Changes have been observed for the better in Russo-American relations," the presidential press service quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.
Asked about Russia's relations with NATO, whose expansion Moscow fiercely opposes as a threat to its own security, Yastrzhembsky said it was premature to speak of a breakthrough.
But he added that Russia hoped to reach some kind of agreement with the Atlantic alliance during a series of talks scheduled for this and next month.
Yeltsin will meet Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov in the Kremlin on Thursday and will make a radio address to the nation on Friday, Yastrzhembsky said.
He is also expected to hold talks with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov early next week on conditions in Russia's cash-strapped armed forces.

Yeltsin will meet Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, probably in the Kremlin, on February 18. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is also expected to visit Moscow in the spring, Yastrzhembsky said.
